Explain why the organizational change is being proposed.
The current College of Education and Professional Studies (CEPS) is composed of three units: the School of Education (SOE), The School of Professional Studies (SPC), and The Office of Strategic Initiatives (OSI).
Ultimately, the proposed change is a change in name based on the dissolution of the two schools with OSI remaining as part of the new College of Education.
This proposal aligns with the new URI strategic plan.
A strong K-12 and higher education system is essential to meeting the strategic vision to “be a leading global research university that drives positive social, economic, and environmental change by contributing and instilling new knowledge to address the world’s greatest challenges.” Excellence and equity in education are among the world's greatest challenges and opportunities.

A recent Hanover Research report (2023) benchmarked the differences between standalone Colleges of Education and Education departments within interdisciplinary colleges and found that standalone colleges have an enrollment growth rate of 3.8% while education programs in interdisciplinary colleges have a declining growth rate of -6.8%.
Further, standalone Colleges of Education are more likely to employ faculty on the tenure track, while programs in interdisciplinary colleges hire an abundance of instructors with no academic rank.
The proposed shift positions URI as the only institution in the state with a standalone College of Education.
The School of Professional Studies (SPC) has very low enrollment in the current degree granting undergraduate programs.
When SPC was created, the university shifted the model of serving adult learners in Providence to serving adult learners better in all programs at URI.
That shift has left four under-enrolled degree programs in SPC.
The CEPS Dean currently has management responsibilities for the Providence campus.
However, the College (CEPS) and campus (Shepard Building) are two separate entities.

This proposal addresses the proposed change to the college unit, not the Providence Campus.
Decisions about the Providence campus building are beyond the scope of this academic unit proposal.
On January 26, 2023, the URI Faculty Senate voted to close two of the four SPC programs (Non-Profit Administration; Professional leadership Studies).
Proposals to move the remaining two programs (BIS-General Studies; BIS-Learner Designed) to Arts and Sciences are currently moving though the faculty senate approval process.
With these closures and moves, there are no remaining academic programs in the School of Professional Studies.
This proposal includes keeping the Office of Strategic Initiatives in the College of Education.
The work that OSI does is in line with educational work in K-12 (e.g., concurrent/dual enrollment) and adult education (e.g., grant work, professional development) systems and thus, makes sense to remain with the new College of Education.
As the college moves forward with a more streamlined emphasis, there will be even more opportunities for synergies within the College of Education.
